plan_prompt:
## Settled design (nobody re-derives it — TRAFFIC-CLASSES §K21 verbatim law)

1. **A channel declaration gains a traffic-class facet**: `durable`
   (today's behaviour, THE DEFAULT — an undeclared class is durable, no
   existing declaration changes meaning) or `transient`.
2. **Transient entries are delivered to live subscribers, never written to
   history, never replayed.** A late joiner does not see past transients,
   and that is honest — they were only ever true in their moment.
3. **Same signing, same verdicts, same schema validation.** Transient is
   about RETENTION, not trust. An unenrolled signer's transient refuses
   exactly as a durable would; malformed refuses; the class changes what
   the store keeps, never what the door accepts.
4. **The derived-state guard is review law**: "would replay-from-empty
   reach the same state? If no, this cannot be transient." The class doc
   carries this test; the package's legs must not put anything
   load-bearing on a transient channel.
5. **Cost honesty (K19)**: transient traffic still crosses the bus and
   still costs delivery. A flooding transient publisher meets the same
   backpressure honesty as anyone — no separate fast lane, no exemption
   from existing flow control.
6. **First consumers pay for the class before any extension uses it**:
   presence and typing indicators for the messaging surface itself
   (survey: "the same K21 class serves the messaging surface").
   Whiteboard strokes are a LATER consumer, not this package.

## What does NOT change (walls inherited from the note)

- No new doors. The compose/declaration doors grow a facet, not a sibling.
- No kernel opinion: which channels are transient is composition-level
  declaration, never a kernel constant or auto-classification.
- K13 blobs and K14 streaming are NOT in this package — separate rungs.
  Nothing here may foreclose them (the open/close-marker + correlation-id
  stream shape from §K14 must remain expressible on a transient channel).
- The record replay contract for durable channels is untouched — the
  package's red-first pins must include a durable-channel replay test that
  passes UNCHANGED before and after.

## Leg topology (fan-out: isolated worktrees, disjoint zones, K8/K9 rig)

- **L1 `transient-class-node`** — OWNS crates/. Content: the declaration
  facet (parse, validate, default-durable); retention enforcement at the
  store boundary (delivered, never written to history, never replayed —
  the PLANNER grounds the exact seam: where append and replay decide);
  refusal-by-name for a transient entry arriving on a channel that
  declared durable-only semantics if the planner finds such a wall exists;
  truth-report disclosure of transient channels (count, class) so the
  class is a visible fact. RED FIRST in-leg: (a) a test pinning that a
  transient entry does NOT survive replay-from-empty while a durable
  sibling does — committed failing against current always-durable
  behaviour; (b) the durable-replay-unchanged pin. Same signing/verdict
  suite green on transient arms. Rust battery green in-leg. Report to
  .fleet/reports/L1.md.
- **L2 `presence-typing-surface`** — OWNS surface/page/. Content: presence
  and typing indicators for the messaging surface riding a declared
  transient channel through the EXISTING send path (session send client —
  K9's one send path; no new transport, no polling); rendering that
  degrades to nothing when no transients arrive (a page without presence
  is merely quiet, never broken); composition-suite claims for
  typing-shows/typing-clears/absent-on-reload (the reload arm IS the
  derived-state guard made visible in the suite). Page battery (tsc,
  composition suite, gate:dist, loc-gate ≤500) green in-leg against the
  ruled facet (door mocked at the contract, as the suite already fakes
  the door). Report to .fleet/reports/L2.md.

Merged-tree gates mine: full Rust battery + full page battery on the
merged tree, then the MANDATORY dev-estate walk at my desk — a scratch
estate through the REAL door: declare a transient channel, two browser
sessions, typing indicator appears live in the second and is GONE after
its reload (the honest late-joiner), durable messages on the same page
replay intact, truth report shows the transient channel. K8's law: only
the walk catches what the live substrate knows. Landing after the walk.
Live estate untouched; page half deploys as a rebuild in the serving
checkout, the Rust half rides the next kernel restart (LANDED IS NOT
RUNNING — said so in the report).

## Hard walls

⛔ Live estate (ports 4176/41100-41102/9490s, every .manifold* path)
untouchable; scratch estates only.
⛔ No weakening of signature judgment on any arm — transient is retention,
not trust (§K21 law).
⛔ Nothing load-bearing on a transient channel — the replay-from-empty
test is the wall, in both legs' suites.
⛔ No new transport, no polling, no timers standing in for delivery.
⛔ No foreclosure of K14: the stream frame shape must remain expressible.

You are the PLANNER of a fleet run. Your working directory is the target repository worktree. Write .fleet/plan.md (the whole plan, every requirement anchored file:line into THIS tree) and one complete builder brief per leg at .fleet/legs/L1.md and .fleet/legs/L2.md. BEFORE minting ANY new name — wire verb paths, refusal names, facet or record kinds, key filenames, topic names — CENSUS the substrate's existing names by searching the crates/ and surface/ trees for collisions, and record in .fleet/plan.md what you searched and what you found: a previous fleet run's brief minted a facet name the registry's own admission door already owned, and only a live estate caught it. For THIS package the planner's grounding duty includes the retention seam: find and anchor file:line where append and replay decide, so L1's store-boundary enforcement lands at the real seam. The legs will run IN PARALLEL, each builder in its own isolated worktree on its own branch — no leg sees another leg's work, and the branches are merged mechanically afterwards. Each brief must therefore be fully self-contained and independent of the other legs' outputs, and must name exactly which files its leg owns so no two legs write the same file; if the settled design forces two legs toward the same file, say so explicitly in .fleet/plan.md and assign that file to exactly one leg. Each brief is floors-not-ceilings, anchored, restates the hard walls above, and names the report file the builder must write (.fleet/reports/<id>.md). You are planning CONTENT for this fixed topology, not changing it. Commit nothing; the .fleet/ files are your only writes. When done, reply with a short summary of the plan you wrote.
